subject: Econ approval lanes & ops gates — next steps
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire@mindlytics.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up & MAP request — latency, hosting, procurement

Hi Michael / Neha,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — we appreciated the walkthrough of the runtime and how Redwood handles routing/fallbacks. A couple quick clarifications that would help our procurement and infra teams: 

- Economic buyer: can you confirm who at Redwood we should include for an official commercial approval (e.g., who signs off on discount / committed capacity)? Our CFO is Mark Delaney and he wants to see a short approval lane.
- Hosting preference: we are leaning toward Dedicated (US-East) for data isolation, but want to understand the tradeoffs vs Private VPC for our compliance team.
- Latency/cost targets: our UX team expects p95 generation latency ~<220ms for 512-token responses; procurement wants a cost-per-1k-tokens ballpark to model TCO.
- Security/compliance: we will send an RFI — can you confirm a point of contact for SOC2 evidence and logging/audit details?

Can you put together a 3–4 step mutual action plan (MAP) with owners and a rough timeline so we can present to procurement next week? I attached a quick procurement contact list (procurement_contact.csv).

Claire
Claire Huang
Head of AI Ops | MindLytics
claire@mindlytics.ai

Attachment: procurement_contact.csv (CSV stub, 1KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@mindlytics.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & MAP request — latency, hosting, procurement

Claire — thanks for the clear list. See a first-pass MAP below and a few answers inline. I attached a draft MAP workbook for your team to edit (redwood_MAP_draft.xlsx) and a short RFI starter (mindlytics_rfi_answers.pdf) with the evidence pointers.

Mutual Action Plan (draft) — high level
1) Internal alignment (MindLytics) — owner: Claire — by 2026-06-16
   - Confirm econ buyer (Mark Delaney) and procurement lead (name on your CSV)
2) Technical evaluation (PoC) — owner: Neha (Redwood SE) & MindLytics infra — 2 weeks
   - Bench: 512-token payloads, p95 target 220ms (pilot config: dedicated us-east pool, x2 GPU nodes)
3) Security & compliance review — owner: Ben (Redwood PS) & MindLytics security — 1 week
   - Share SOC2 artifacts, logging/audit scoping, data retention options
4) Commercial/contracting — owner: Michael (Redwood sales lead) & MindLytics procurement — target NBO within 30 days post-PoC

Quick answers:
- Econ approval: yes, Michael Grant will be the Redwood commercial approver for discounts and committed capacity; legal counter-signs.
- Hosting: Dedicated simplifies the onboarding timeline; Private VPC is available but adds network and account setup time (2–3 extra weeks). We'll note both options in the MAP.
- Latency/cost: we'll run a short benchmark during PoC and provide cost-per-1k estimate. For planning, internal comps suggest ~ $XX–YY per 1k tokens depending on batching/quantization — we will firm that up.
- SOC2/evidence: Ben will be primary; Ben — I linked the RFI starter and points to the SOC2 report in the Drive.

Next steps:
- Claire: confirm econ buyer + procurement lead on your side so we can lock owners in the MAP.
- Neha/Ben: I’ll schedule the PoC kickoff for next Tue/Wed — ping me your availability.

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_MAP_draft.xlsx (workbook, 12KB); mindlytics_rfi_answers.pdf (PDF stub, 38KB)

Michael — appreciate the MAP draft and the RFI starter. A couple of updates from procurement/security: 

- Procurement contact: Jessica Park (jessica.park@mindlytics.ai) — she’s the lead and expects formal vendor terms/questions this week.
- Econ buyer: CFO Mark Delaney (mark.delaney@mindlytics.ai) — he wants a 1-page approval lane showing sign-off thresholds (who approves up to $X, who approves larger).
- Timeline: procurement wants the PoC results and RFI answers by 2026-06-23 to route to finance for an EOY budget tranche.
- Hosting: on balance they prefer Dedicated in US-East to avoid cross-VPC routing; compliance will accept Dedicated if logging/audit and key management meet their checklist.
- Latency/cost tolerance: product can accept p95 <=250ms for 512 tokens if we can show consistent p95 in PoC; procurement wants cost banding (low/expected/high usage) to model billing.

We will put Jessica on the thread. She may send a formal vendor questionnaire.

Claire

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: negotiation lanes & prep for PoC kickoff (private)

Neha / Ben — internal checklist before we kick off PoC next week (private notes):

- Econ lanes: prepare a 1-pager showing approval thresholds. We should propose two commercial paths: (A) 6–12 month Dedicated commit with a small onboarding credit + ramp discount, (B) Private VPC with one-time onboarding fee and no commit. Set suggested discount tiers for A (5% at <$50k/mo, 10% at <$150k/mo, 15% >$150k/mo).
- Technical scope: Neha, confirm test corpus + expected concurrency so bench matches MindLytics UX cases (512 tokens, p95 target 220–250ms). Include KV cache/batching knobs.
- Compliance: Ben, pull the SOC2 section that shows logging/audit retention and KMS integrations; have the artifact ready to upload.
- Risk/SLAs: we should be prepared to offer p95 SLA for Dedicated; identify exceptions (burst capacity, scheduled maintenance). Draft a fallback policy (model variant to cheaper instance) and cost impact note.

Action owners:
- Neha: PoC plan + bench config by MON 06/14
- Ben: SOC2 artifacts + RFI answers by TUE 06/15
- Michael: commercial proposal skeleton & MAP update by TUE 06/15

Keep this internal — will tidy language before we share back to Claire/Jessica.

Thanks,
Michael
